feed.title: Google Cloud: Network Security Integration
feed.subtitle: Changelog for Google Cloud product: Network Security Integration

entry.content:
The broker mode for out-of-band Network Security Integration (also known as packet broker) is now available in General Availability (GA) with allowlist. Broker mode lets you mirror GENEVE-encapsulated network packets from a consumer network to multiple producer networks for analysis, and adds additional GENEVE metadata (such as timestamp and network stable ID). This feature is not available to all users. To access this feature, contact your Google account team.

For more information, see Out-of-band integration overview and Understand GENEVE format.
entry.summary: Broker mode for out-of-band Network Security Integration is now in General Availability with allowlist. This feature allows mirroring of GENEVE-encapsulated network packets for analysis and adds extra GENEVE metadata. Contact your Google account team to access this feature.
entry.title: Feature: Packet Broker Mode Now Available

entry.content:
Project-level security profiles and security profile groups for Network Security Integration are now available in General Availability (GA).

For more information, see Security profiles overview and Security profile groups overview.
entry.summary: Project-level security profiles and security profile groups for Network Security Integration have reached General Availability. This feature enhances network security management by allowing for more granular control at the project level. Explore the overview documentation for more details on implementation and benefits.
entry.title: Feature: Network Security Profiles Now Generally Available

entry.content: You can now enable zonal affinity for your Network Security Integration in-band integration deployments and configure zonal interception with regional backends. For more information, see Zonal affinity.
entry.summary: You can now enable zonal affinity for your Network Security Integration in-band integration deployments. This feature allows you to configure zonal interception with regional backends, providing more control over your network traffic routing.
entry.title: Feature: Zonal Affinity for Network Security Integration

entry.content: You can now integrate your network security appliances directly in the network traffic path for inspection and identify any threats before the traffic reaches its destination. For more information, see In-band integration overview. This feature is available in General Availability.
entry.summary: You can now integrate your network security appliances directly in the network traffic path for inspection and identify any threats before the traffic reaches its destination. This feature is available in General Availability.
entry.title: Feature: Integrate network security appliances

entry.content: Network Security integration now retains 396 bytes for the GENEVE encapsulation overhead. Consumer networks must use the maximum transmission unit (MTU) size of 8500 bytes or less. Producer networks must use an MTU at least 396 bytes more than the consumer network. For more information, see GENEVE encapsulation and MTU requirements.
entry.summary: The GENEVE encapsulation overhead has been updated to 396 bytes. Ensure your network's MTU is set appropriately to avoid issues. Consumer networks should use an MTU of 8500 bytes or less, while producer networks need an MTU at least 396 bytes larger than the consumer network's MTU.
entry.title: Changed: Network Security: GENEVE Encapsulation Overhead Update
